rules: Use the existing Marion MonIA atlas pack as the identity authority.
Do not redesign, substitute or beautify Marion into a different woman.
Preserve facial proportions, eyes, smile, hair and recognizable appearance across close-up, medium and full-body shots.
Use full-body framing when the gameplay scene requires walking, posture or environmental interaction.
Generate cinematic gameplay media in 16:9 desktop format by default.
Never replace a validated Marion media asset without explicit approval.
Use only the canonical Lucas source video and extracted canon frames as identity references.
Use the canonical Lucas source video as the movement reference whenever the generation backend supports video guidance.
When direct video guidance is unavailable, derive motion cues from the canonical source video rather than inventing a different manner of moving.
Do not redesign or substitute Lucas.
Preserve facial geometry, hair, eyes, stubble, skin tone, neck and chest tattoos.
Preserve natural ears exactly as the source; no holes, gauges, piercings, earrings or invented ear details.
Use full-body framing when the gameplay scene requires walking, posture or environmental interaction.
Generate candidates only in 16:9 desktop format.
Never replace the approved live Lucas video without explicit user approval.

gameplayMediaRules: Dynamic gameplay cinematics must use the locked Marion and Lucas reference packs whenever either character appears.
Do not generate a named character from text alone when a canonical pack exists.
Prefer subtle believable movement over large gestures when identity preservation is at risk.
Keep generated media as candidates until validated; gameplay must fall back to already approved media rather than publish an identity-drifted result.
Default cinematic gameplay composition is 16:9 desktop.
